as_of: exercise day11; all four released stages, no oracle
decision: Continue the bounded coordination case; do not mark all fixed. Record separate completed milestones for U's validated release, Cedar distribution and one verified customer installation, while retaining the second deployment's protection gap and scoped inventory questions. Immediately correct the local incident-count drafts and prepare a narrowly scoped protective update for operator approval. Closure should be per evidenced workstream, not a single all-fixed label or an impossible demand to prove every imaginable fork safe.

evidence_ledger.subject: U and Cedar repair
evidence_ledger.fact: Cedar distributes its repair to customer administrators
evidence_ledger.assessment: U validated release remains supported; Cedar product package has now progressed from prepared to distributed. Delivery receipts for both incident customers demonstrate delivery, not installation.

evidence_ledger.subject: customer protection
evidence_ledger.fact: only one has supplied a verified installation receipt
evidence_ledger.assessment: One customer has evidence of repair installation; the other only has a day12 plan. Do not infer the latter is installed, currently protected, or will certainly install on schedule. Installation evidence supports that repair milestone, not a guarantee against all compromise.

evidence_ledger.subject: second customer's mitigation
evidence_ledger.fact: Its local operator rejects that mitigation pending an acceptable continuity plan
evidence_ledger.assessment: Feature-disable option has unacceptable essential-workflow cost in this deployment under current assessment. Do not continue blanket advice to disable it. No validated alternative exists here; unresolved protection and continuity tradeoff needs accountable action, not an invented safe workaround.

evidence_ledger.subject: incident evidence
evidence_ledger.fact: one of the two events was a misclassified test; the other remains independently corroborated actual misuse
evidence_ledger.assessment: Correct supported count to one actual misuse event/deployment from the original two-event set, with the withdrawn test classification retained in history. Do not retract all concern or keep two as current. The packet does not identify whether the remaining actual misuse belongs to the installed or not-yet-installed customer; do not infer that association.

evidence_ledger.subject: public exposure
evidence_ledger.fact: The recording remains authenticated public exposure
evidence_ledger.assessment: Partial public exposure remains established independently of incident correction; raw packet restrictions remain unchanged.

evidence_ledger.subject: Birch
evidence_ledger.fact: authenticated B-legacy inventory assessment covering standard edition L1 only: the relevant path is absent there
evidence_ledger.assessment: Narrow B-legacy uncertainty for standard L1 under that assessment only. Prior surveyed B-current exclusion remains. Custom fork attachment does not establish an active installed/owned vulnerable fork; other legacy editions are outside supplied evidence. Do not call all legacy safe or assert custom-fork affectedness.

evidence_ledger.subject: coordination
evidence_ledger.fact: Harbor accepts the common lead and proposes correcting the incident count in its planned advisory
evidence_ledger.assessment: Lead alignment stands; advisory is still planned, not already published. North's all-fixed question is a proposal unsupported by separate deployment evidence. Neither coordinator has publication authority from this exercise.

owners_and_next_actions: North: maintain separate product-repair, customer-protection, scope and communication workstreams; reject the all-fixed shortcut. Obtain explicit closure criteria for the known case and document residual unknowns without asserting universal ecosystem coverage.

Cedar/Ivo and second customer's local operator: jointly resolve continuity constraints and verify the day12 installation outcome, or record why delayed and an accountable next checkpoint. Do not override the local operator or invent an alternative mitigation. Cedar can support feasibility/validation; the customer owns local operational acceptance. First customer's installation evidence closes that milestone only.

Defender with Cedar: record reason/provenance for reclassification, retain the original assessment plus correction, clarify which deployment retains confirmed misuse if needed for protection prioritization. Do not assume the uninstalled deployment is the exploited one.

Rhea: retain standard L1 assessment scope, identify whether the custom-fork attachment represents an active installed product and seek the appropriate technical owner if it does. Rhea's inventory role is not a broad affectedness signature. North tracks remaining legacy scope explicitly rather than making unsupported all-editions claims.

North and Harbor: align corrected count and current protection states in their planned drafts. If any earlier authorized real-world communication had existed, identify its recipients and prepare a linked correction, but this exercise supplies none and no publication is performed. Raw-material permissions remain owned separately by Fenn/Cedar.
information_boundaries: Do not circulate restricted reproducer or Cedar customer excerpt to Harbor or publicly. Lead consensus, published component/precondition and an incident-count correction do not change the allowed recipient sets. Use a minimum permission-cleared summary for any proposed notice; avoid individual-customer details that are not necessary or approved. Preserve factual correction internally with access restrictions, not raw evidence dumping.

timing_and_alternatives.checkpoint: Prepare corrected drafts on day11 before any planned advisory is approved. Keep a day12 checkpoint tied to actual installation evidence and continuity outcome at the second customer, not simply arrival of its scheduled date. Escalate earlier for new corroborated misuse or failed protection plans. If day12 evidence is absent, explicitly retain the gap and assign a bounded next checkpoint rather than mark completed.
timing_and_alternatives.why: Distribution and one installation reduce specific open work, but one customer's unverified repair and operationally unsuitable mitigation mean known protection work remains. Corroborated misuse remains despite correction, so silence or all-fixed closure would mislead. Unknown custom-fork existence is a different, investigative residual, not proof of additional victims.
timing_and_alternatives.alternative: Administratively close the product-release workstream now with a clearly linked, separately owned deployment/continuity and inventory follow-up case. That can avoid blocking completed engineering work on every uncertain fork. Downside: a broad closure label may hide the second customer's actual protection gap or orphan ownership; accept only with explicit residual owners/checkpoints and no all-fixed public claim. Keep overall coordination open until that handoff is evidenced.
timing_and_alternatives.rejected: Either declaring all fixed from release/delivery or retracting all security concern after one misclassification erases supported remaining risk. Keeping the old two-confirmed figure is equally wrong.

minimum_information_handoff: LOCAL CORRECTED NOTICE DRAFT, NOT PUBLISHED: The earlier assessment of two confirmed misuse events has been corrected: one was a misclassified test, while one remains independently corroborated misuse of the Cedar S weakness. Authenticated partial public exposure remains. U's repaired component is released and Cedar has distributed its product repair; installation is verified for one of the two tracked customers, not both. The temporary feature-disable mitigation is unsuitable for an essential workflow at the other tracked customer without an acceptable continuity plan, and no alternative is yet validated there. Surveyed Birch B-current and assessed standard legacy L1 exclude the relevant path within their assessment scope; other legacy editions/custom-fork deployment and affectedness are unresolved. Proposed next status checkpoint: day12. Final public text may omit customer counts/details unless necessary and approved, but must not imply universal installation or safe blanket disablement. No technical mechanism, restricted abstract/excerpt or unsupported vulnerable-fork claim.
closure_criteria: For a bounded handoff, retain dated evidence of each milestone, actual second-customer installation or an explicitly accepted supported protection/continuity disposition, named owners and scope for unresolved legacy inventory, and aligned corrected advisory drafts/authorized communication disposition. Do not equate coordination closure with every possible ecosystem consumer fixed. A residual can be transferred only with explicit ownership and limitations; no such completed handoff is established here.
transition: Stage3's two-confirmed assessment was defensible on then-supplied corroboration; new correction changes the current count, not the old first response. Stage3's undistributed Cedar status changes to distributed only because new receipts exist; one installation is now evidenced. Its customer-specific mitigation caveat becomes a concrete contraindication at the second deployment. Legacy unknown narrows to an assessed standard L1 subset; other editions/custom fork remain unresolved. Urgent scoped protective communication, public-exposure fact, independent downstream deployment reasoning and raw-material restrictions remain justified. Earlier screenshot was never authenticated by these later events.
